skill.name: convex-setup-auth
skill.description: Sets up authentication for Convex apps. It guides provider selection, client wiring, backend identity checks, user mapping, and authorization. Supports Convex Auth, Clerk, WorkOS AuthKit, Auth0, and custom JWT providers.
skill.summary: Add secure login and Convex identity checks with provider-specific setup guidance.
skill.author: get-convex

content.value_statement: Convex auth setup can fail when provider wiring, environment variables, and backend checks do not match. This skill guides the correct provider flow and adds verified Convex authentication patterns.
actual_capabilities: Helps choose between Convex Auth, Clerk, WorkOS AuthKit, Auth0, and custom JWT providers.
Guides setup of convex/auth.config.ts and provider-specific client wrappers.
Explains required environment variables for local and production authentication setup.
Shows how to protect Convex queries and mutations with ctx.auth.getUserIdentity().
Covers optional user table mapping and role-based access control when the app needs it.
Provides validation checklists for sign-in, Convex auth state, and protected backend functions.
limitations: Requires user confirmation when provider accounts, dashboard actions, or CLI logins are interactive.
Does not replace current provider documentation; it directs the agent to verify official docs.
Cannot validate production tenants unless required credentials and deployment access are available.
May need manual checks when browser automation is unavailable.

use_cases.title: Connect an existing auth provider

prompt_templates.title: Add basic login
prompt_templates.prompt: Add authentication to this Convex app. Ask me which provider to use if the repo does not make it clear.

prompt_templates.title: Wire an existing provider
prompt_templates.prompt: This app already uses Clerk. Connect it to Convex auth, preserve the current sign-in flow, and verify Convex sees authenticated users.

prompt_templates.title: Protect backend functions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Convex queries and mutations. Add server-side identity checks and authorization for user-owned records where needed.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare production auth
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure production-ready Convex authentication for WorkOS AuthKit. Separate dev and production settings, then provide a validation checklist.

output_examples.input: Set up auth for a new Convex app with Convex Auth.
output_examples.output: Provider decision recorded, required setup steps completed, client provider wired, protected backend checks added, and local sign-in validation listed.

output_examples.input: Connect Clerk to an existing Convex app.
output_examples.output: The response identifies existing Clerk files, updates Convex auth wiring, confirms required environment values, and lists sign-in tests.

output_examples.input: Make this Convex app production-ready for Auth0.
output_examples.output: The result separates local and production tenant settings, checks redirect URLs, and warns when Auth0 token validation needs manual review.

best_practices: Choose the auth provider before writing setup code.
Use official provider documentation for current package and CLI steps.
Verify both frontend login and ctx.auth.getUserIdentity() in Convex functions.
anti_patterns: Do not trust client-provided user IDs for protected data.
Do not add a users table unless the app needs app-level user records.
Do not claim setup is complete until Convex recognizes the authenticated session.

faq.question: Which providers does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Convex Auth, Clerk, WorkOS AuthKit, Auth0, and custom JWT provider setup for Convex apps.

faq.question: Can it create provider accounts for me?
faq.answer: It can guide dashboard or CLI setup, but users must complete account sign-in and interactive approvals.

faq.question: Does every app need a Convex users table?
faq.answer: No. The skill recommends app-level user records only when the product needs them.

faq.question: Can it handle production setup?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks for production intent and checks provider values, redirect URLs, and Convex deployment settings.

faq.question: Does it store secrets?
faq.answer: The skill describes required environment variables. Secrets should stay in provider dashboards, local env files, or Convex environment settings.

faq.question: How does it validate setup?
faq.answer: It checks sign-in, Convex auth state, protected queries, backend identity, and production settings when requested.
